Unit 1 of 10: Basic Computer Organisation

Key ideas

  • A computer accepts input, processes it according to instructions and produces output; it can also store data.
  • Input devices: keyboard, mouse, scanner, microphone. Output devices: monitor, printer, speaker.
  • CPU (Central Processing Unit): the "brain" — ALU (arithmetic and logic operations), CU (control unit — directs operations) and registers (very fast small storage).
  • Hardware: physical parts. Software: programs and instructions.
  • Data moves between memory and CPU through buses (data, address and control).

Worked examples

Example 1: Which part of the CPU compares two numbers? Answer: the ALU (logic operations include comparison).

10-mark practice set

  1. (1 mark, MCQ) The part of the CPU that directs all operations is the: (a) ALU (b) CU (c) RAM (d) ROM. Answer: (b).
  2. (1 mark) Name one output device. Answer: monitor (or printer, speaker).
  3. (2 marks) Name the two main units of the CPU and one job of each. Answer: ALU — calculations and comparisons (1); CU — controls and coordinates operations (1).
  4. (3 marks) Classify as input or output: scanner, speaker, microphone. Answer: input (1); output (1); input (1).
  5. (3 marks) Name the three types of bus and what each carries. Answer: data bus — data (1); address bus — memory addresses (1); control bus — control signals (1).

Common mistakes

  1. CPU = cabinet. 2. ALU and CU swapped. 3. Touchscreen only output (it's both). 4. Hardware/software confused. 5. Missing buses.

Quick recall

  1. Brain? 2. Calculations? 3. Controls? 4. Fast CPU storage? 5. Physical parts?

Answers: 1) CPU. 2) ALU. 3) CU. 4) Registers. 5) Hardware.
